title: Transporting the Past: An Optimal Transport View of Backtracking Counterfactuals
claim: Pointwise projection of posterior atoms onto the constraint set breaks exogenous independence; our independence-constrained transport preserves it.
layout: 4 scatter panels in two example groups, OT-CF versus IOT-CF side by side
description: Four 2-D scatter plots in the exogenous space (U1, U2), grouped into two examples. Example 1 is a quadratic SCM and Example 2 is a multimodal SCM. In each example, the left panel shows the OT-CF distribution and the right panel shows the IOT-CF distribution. Red dots mark observed posterior atoms. A thick black closed curve marks the counterfactual constraint set. In the left panels, blue diamonds sit on the curve near the red dots, with small gray arrows showing the pointwise projection. Some are annotated with x3^CF values. In the right panels, green stars sit on the curve in a configuration that preserves independence. In Example 1 the stars are at (0, ±√2). The shared legend sits below the panels, and the eye goes first to the colored markers on the black curve.
caption: Illustrative backtracking counterfactuals in exogenous space. Red points denote posterior atoms compatible with the factual observation, blue diamonds denote OT-CF atoms, green stars denote IOT-CF atoms, and black curves denote the counterfactual constraint set $x_2^{\mathrm{CF}}=2$. In OT-CF, posterior atoms are projected pointwise to nearby feasible points on the constraint set. In IOT-CF, the transported counterfactual distribution is constrained to preserve exogenous independence.
abstract: We study backtracking counterfactual inference for Structural Causal Models (SCMs) through the lens of optimal transport. In SCMs, a factual observation generally induces a posterior distribution over exogenous variables, making counterfactual inference inherently distributional. We introduce two complementary frameworks that transport this posterior onto the set of exogenous configurations satisfying a desired counterfactual query. The first constructs a natural pointwise projection and is suitable when the transported exogenous distribution can be used directly. The second enforces mutual independence among counterfactual exogenous variables, so that the transported variables remain interpretable as genuine exogenous noises of the same SCM. We show that both frameworks are consistent with the original backtracking counterfactual principle, and we propose marginal, penalty-based, and hard-constrained solvers for finite-posterior settings. Synthetic experiments on non-bijective SCMs illustrate the geometry of the problem and reveal trade-offs among transport cost, counterfactual constraint satisfaction, and preservation of exogenous independence.
